title: Specification of the consequential requirements with respect to Amendment of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Merchant Bankers) Regulations, 1992

extraction.subject: Amendment of SEBI (Merchant Bankers) Regulations, 1992
extraction.summary: The circular introduces amendments to the SEBI (Merchant Bankers) Regulations, 1992, focusing on revised capital adequacy, liquid net worth requirements, and other compliance obligations for Merchant Bankers. These changes aim to enhance financial stability and operational transparency within the merchant banking sector.

obligations.action: Fulfill revised capital adequacy and liquid net worth requirements.
obligations.deadline: As on date of application for new applicants; phased manner for existing MBs.
obligations.notes: Phased implementation for existing MBs as per Table I.

obligations.action: Categorize as Category I or II and submit Chartered Accountant certified Net worth Certificate.
obligations.penalty_for_non_compliance: Automatic designation as Category II or restriction on activities.
obligations.notes: Includes liquid net worth component.

obligations.action: Submit Chartered Accountant certificate as part of Half Yearly Report.
obligations.notes: Certifies net worth and liquid net worth maintenance.

obligations.action: Comply with underwriting obligations not exceeding 20 times liquid net worth.
obligations.notes: Includes Chartered Accountant certification.

obligations.action: Ensure employees and compliance officer obtain requisite certifications.
obligations.deadline: On or before January 02, 2027 for existing employees; within 90 days of appointment for new employees.
obligations.notes: NISM Series-IX and Series-IIIA certifications required.

obligations.action: Ensure compliance officer is independent from other employees.
obligations.notes: Applies to existing MBs.

obligations.action: Ensure principal officer has relevant experience.
obligations.notes: Five years of experience in financial markets required.

obligations.action: Close outsourced core merchant banking activities.
obligations.notes: Applies to existing MBs with open mandates.

obligations.action: Generate minimum revenue from permitted activities.
obligations.penalty_for_non_compliance: Certificate of registration liable to be cancelled.
obligations.notes: Minimum revenue thresholds specified for Category I and II.

obligations.action: Submit revenue details to SEBI.
obligations.deadline: Within three months from the end of each financial year, starting FY 2026-27
obligations.notes: Applies to revenue from permitted activities.

obligations.action: Disclose involvement in marketing of issues where holding exceeds specified limits.
obligations.deadline: Applicable to public issues filed on or after January 03, 2026
obligations.notes: Disclosure in offer document and marketing material required.

obligations.action: Segregate non-SEBI regulated activities into separate business units.
obligations.notes: Chinese Wall and ring-fencing required.

obligations.action: Disclose non-SEBI regulated activities on website.
obligations.notes: Disclosure of non-availability of SEBI protection mechanisms required.

obligations.action: Submit compliance report for non-SEBI regulated activities.
obligations.notes: Includes confirmation/acknowledgement from stakeholders.

key_thresholds.value: Rs. 25 cr (Phase I), Rs. 50 cr (Phase II)

key_thresholds.parameter: Liquid net worth for Category I
key_thresholds.value: Rs. 6.25 cr (Phase I), Rs. 12.5 cr (Phase II)
Rs. 7.5 cr (Phase I), Rs. 10 cr (Phase II)

key_thresholds.parameter: Liquid net worth for Category II
key_thresholds.value: Rs. 1.875 cr (Phase I), Rs. 2.5 cr (Phase II)

key_thresholds.context: Cumulative over three preceding financial years
Cumulative over three preceding financial years

extraction.risk_rationale: The circular introduces significant changes to capital and operational requirements, impacting the financial and operational stability of Merchant Bankers.

title: Revised Norms for appointment of an independent third-party reviewer/ certifier for green debt security

extraction.subject: Revised Norms for appointment of an independent third-party reviewer/certifier for green debt security
extraction.summary: This circular modifies the requirements for appointing an independent third-party reviewer/certifier for green debt securities to align with those for social and sustainability bonds. It specifies the conditions under which the reviewer must operate and the forms the review may take.

obligations.action: Appoint an independent third-party reviewer/certifier to ascertain compliance with the definition of green debt securities and review/certify processes.
obligations.section_reference: Regulation 2(1)(q) of the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021
obligations.notes: Reviewer must be independent of issuer and have expertise in ESG debt securities.

obligations.action: Ensure the scope of the review by the independent third-party reviewer is specified in the offer document.
Ensure details regarding the independent third-party reviewer are adequately disclosed in the offer document.

amendments_to.specific_provisions: Chapter IX, Paragraph 1.8 deleted and new Paragraph 5 inserted

extraction.risk_rationale: The changes require issuers to engage independent reviewers, which may involve additional compliance costs and processes.

extraction.subject: Revision of Order-to-Trade Ratio (OTR) framework
extraction.summary: The circular revises the Order-to-Trade Ratio (OTR) framework for stock exchanges, exempting certain orders from penalties. It aims to address concerns raised by stakeholders and improve market efficiency.

applies_to.entity_type: Recognized Stock Exchanges (except Commodity Derivative Stock Exchanges)

obligations.action: Make necessary amendments to the relevant bye-laws, rules and regulations for the implementation of the above decision.
obligations.notes: Applies to stock exchanges for implementing the revised OTR framework.

obligations.action: Bring the provisions of this circular to the notice of the market participants (including TMs) and disseminate the same on their website.
obligations.notes: Ensures market participants are informed of the changes.

key_thresholds.parameter: Order price range for equity option contracts
key_thresholds.value: ±40% of LTP (premium) or ±INR 20, whichever is higher
key_thresholds.context: Exempted from the framework for imposing penalty for high OTR.

key_thresholds.parameter: Order price range for other orders
key_thresholds.context: Exempted from the framework for imposing penalty for high OTR.

supersedes.description: Modifies specific paragraphs related to the OTR framework.

amendments_to.regulation_name: Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations

extraction.risk_rationale: The changes affect trading operations and require stock exchanges to update their systems and inform participants, but do not introduce new penalties.

title: Late Submission Fee for reporting delays under Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA)

extraction.effective_date: immediately for the delayed filings made on or after the date of this circular
extraction.subject: Late Submission Fee for reporting delays under Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA)
extraction.summary: The circular introduces a uniform Late Submission Fee (LSF) structure for reporting delays under FEMA, applicable to various forms and returns. It aims to standardize penalties for late submissions across different types of foreign investment and borrowing reports.

obligations.action: Calculate and impose LSF for reporting delays using the specified matrix.
obligations.deadline: immediately for the delayed filings made on or after the date of this circular
obligations.penalty_for_non_compliance: liable for penal action under the provisions of FEMA, 1999
obligations.section_reference: section 10(4) and 11(1) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999
obligations.notes: LSF is applicable per return, with specific calculations for different forms.

obligations.action: Bring the contents of this circular to the notice of constituents and customers.

key_thresholds.context: LSF amount will be limited to 100 per cent of ‘A’ and rounded upwards to the nearest hundred.

amendments_to.regulation_name: Master Direction – Reporting under Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999
Master Direction - External Commercial Borrowings, Trade Credits and Structured Obligations

extraction.risk_rationale: The introduction of a standardized LSF structure increases the financial risk for non-compliance with reporting deadlines.

title: Master Direction - Non-Banking Financial Companies Auditor’s Report (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2016

extraction.subject: Non-Banking Financial Companies Auditor’s Report (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2016
extraction.summary: The RBI has issued new directions for auditors of non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), superseding the 2008 directions. These directions require auditors to submit additional reports to the Board of Directors and exception reports to the RBI, ensuring compliance with various financial and regulatory criteria.

obligations.action: Auditors must submit a separate report to the Board of Directors on specified matters.
obligations.deadline: for every financial year ending on any day on or after the commencement of these Directions
obligations.section_reference: Section 143 of the Companies Act, 2013 or section 227 of the Companies Act, 1956
obligations.notes: This is in addition to the report made under the Companies Act.

obligations.action: Auditors must submit an exception report to the RBI if the auditor's report is unfavorable or qualified.
obligations.section_reference: Chapter III B of RBI Act, Non-Banking Financial Companies Acceptance of Public Deposits Directions, 2016, Non-Systemically Important Non-Deposit taking Company Directions, 2016, Systemically Important Non-Deposit taking Company and Deposit taking Company Directions, 2016
obligations.notes: The report should contain details of unfavorable or qualified statements and non-compliance.

key_thresholds.value: as laid down in relevant Master Directions
key_thresholds.context: For NBFCs to continue holding a Certificate of Registration

supersedes.description: Non-Banking Financial Companies Auditor’s Report (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2008

amendments_to.regulation_name: Non-Banking Financial Company – Non-Systemically Important Non-Deposit taking Company (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2016
Non-Banking Financial Company - Systemically Important Non-Deposit taking Company and Deposit taking Company (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2016

extraction.risk_rationale: Non-compliance could lead to significant regulatory action and impact the ability of NBFCs to operate legally.

title: Guidelines on Digital Lending

extraction.subject: Guidelines on Digital Lending
extraction.summary: The circular provides detailed guidelines for digital lending by regulated entities, emphasizing customer protection, data privacy, and compliance with existing regulations. It aims to ensure transparency and accountability in digital lending processes, impacting both new and existing digital loans.

applies_to.entity_type: Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks, State Co-operative Banks, District Central Co-operative Banks
Non-Banking Financial Companies (including Housing Finance Companies)

obligations.action: Ensure all loan servicing, repayment, etc., is executed directly in the RE’s bank account without any third-party pass-through account.
obligations.notes: Disbursements must be made directly to the borrower's bank account, with specific exceptions.

obligations.action: Ensure fees/charges payable to LSPs are paid directly by REs and not charged to the borrower.
Disclose penal interest/charges upfront on an annualized basis in the Key Fact Statement (KFS).
Provide a Key Fact Statement (KFS) to the borrower before contract execution in a standardized format.
obligations.notes: KFS must include APR, recovery mechanism, grievance redressal officer details, and cooling-off period.

obligations.action: Ensure digitally signed documents flow to borrowers automatically upon loan contract execution.
obligations.notes: Documents include KFS, loan product summary, sanction letter, terms and conditions, etc.

obligations.action: Publish the list of DLAs, LSPs, and their activities on the RE's website.
Ensure DLAs display product information prominently at onboarding/sign-up stage.
Communicate details of the LSP acting as recovery agent to the borrower at loan sanctioning and when recovery responsibilities change.
Ensure DLAs have links to REs’ website for detailed information about loan products and customer care.
obligations.notes: Details must be available at a prominent single place on the website.

obligations.action: Ensure a suitable nodal grievance redressal officer is available for digital lending complaints.
obligations.notes: Contact details must be prominently displayed on websites and in the KFS.

obligations.action: Capture the economic profile of borrowers before extending any loan to assess creditworthiness.
obligations.notes: Profile includes age, occupation, income, etc.

obligations.action: Provide an explicit option for borrowers to exit digital loans during the cooling-off period without penalty.
obligations.notes: Cooling-off period must be at least three days for loans of seven days or more, and one day for shorter loans.

obligations.action: Conduct enhanced due diligence before partnering with LSPs for digital lending.
obligations.notes: Consider technical abilities, data privacy policies, and compliance capabilities.

obligations.action: Ensure data collection by DLAs is need-based and with prior explicit consent of the borrower.
obligations.notes: DLAs must not access mobile phone resources without explicit consent.

obligations.action: Ensure LSPs/DLAs do not store personal information of borrowers except minimal data required for operations.
obligations.notes: Data privacy and security responsibility lies with the RE.

obligations.action: Ensure all data is stored only in servers located within India.
obligations.notes: Must comply with statutory obligations and regulatory instructions.

obligations.action: Ensure DLAs and LSPs have a comprehensive privacy policy compliant with applicable laws and RBI guidelines.
obligations.notes: Privacy policy must be publicly available.

obligations.action: Report any lending done through DLAs to Credit Information Companies (CICs).
obligations.notes: Includes structured digital lending products and deferred payment credits.

key_thresholds.value: Not less than three days for loans of seven days or more, and one day for loans of less than seven days
key_thresholds.context: Period during which a borrower can exit a digital loan without penalty

amendments_to.regulation_name: Master Direction – Reserve Bank of India (Securitisation of Standard Assets) Directions, 2021
amendments_to.specific_provisions: Adherence to provisions regarding First Loss Default Guarantee (FLDG) and synthetic securitisation.

extraction.risk_rationale: The circular introduces comprehensive guidelines for digital lending, impacting a wide range of financial entities and requiring significant changes to existing processes and systems.

repealed_by: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025

title: Review of Regulatory Framework for Housing Finance Companies (HFCs)

extraction.effective_date: from the date of this circular
extraction.subject: Review of regulatory framework for Housing Finance Companies (HFCs)
extraction.summary: The RBI has revised the regulatory framework for Housing Finance Companies (HFCs), superseding certain NHB regulations. Key changes include new definitions and criteria for HFCs, phased compliance timelines, and specific guidelines on liquidity and risk management. This aims to harmonize HFC and NBFC regulations over the next two years.

obligations.action: Submit a Board approved plan including a roadmap to fulfil the criteria and timeline for transition.
obligations.penalty_for_non_compliance: HFCs unable to fulfil the criteria shall be treated as NBFC – Investment and Credit Companies (NBFC-ICC) and will be required to approach the Reserve Bank for conversion of their Certificate of Registration.
obligations.notes: Applies to registered HFCs not currently fulfilling the criteria.

obligations.action: Submit a statutory auditor's certificate to Reserve Bank evidencing compliance with the prescribed NOF levels.
obligations.deadline: within a period of one month
obligations.penalty_for_non_compliance: HFCs failing to achieve the prescribed level shall not be eligible to hold the Certificate of Registration (CoR) as HFCs and registration shall be liable to be cancelled.
obligations.notes: Applies to HFCs with NOF below Rupees twenty crore.

obligations.action: Maintain a Loan to Value (LTV) ratio of 50% for loans granted against the collateral of shares.
obligations.deadline: Any shortfall in the maintenance of the 50% LTV occurring on account of movement in the share prices shall be made good within seven working days.
obligations.section_reference: Para 22 of Master Direction – Non-Banking Financial Company – Systemically Important Non-Deposit taking Company and Deposit taking Company (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2016

obligations.action: Maintain a Loan-to-Value (LTV) Ratio not exceeding 75 per cent for loans granted against the collateral of gold jewellery.
obligations.section_reference: Para 27 and Para 39 of Master Direction – Non-Banking Financial Company – Systemically Important Non-Deposit taking Company and Deposit taking Company (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2016
obligations.notes: HFCs shall put in place a Board approved policy for lending against gold.

obligations.action: Not impose foreclosure charges/ pre-payment penalties on any floating rate term loan sanctioned for purposes other than business to individual borrowers.
obligations.section_reference: Para 31 (4) of Master Direction – Non-Banking Financial Company – Systemically Important Non-Deposit taking Company and Deposit taking Company (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2016

obligations.action: Maintain a liquidity buffer in terms of LCR to promote resilience to potential liquidity disruptions.
obligations.deadline: From December 01, 2021, with phased increases until December 01, 2025
obligations.section_reference: Para 15B of Master Direction - Non-Banking Financial Company - Systemically Important Non-Deposit taking Company and Deposit taking Company (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2016
obligations.notes: Applies to HFCs based on asset size and deposit-taking status.

key_thresholds.parameter: Minimum percentage of total assets towards housing finance
Minimum percentage of total assets towards housing finance for individuals

key_thresholds.context: Required to commence or carry on the business of housing finance

supersedes.circular_reference: Relevant regulations issued by National Housing Bank (NHB)
supersedes.description: Supersession of NHB regulations as per the Annex

extraction.risk_rationale: The circular introduces significant changes to the regulatory framework for HFCs, requiring substantial compliance efforts and potential restructuring.

extraction.subject: Merchanting Trade Transactions (MTT) – Revised Guidelines
extraction.summary: The RBI has revised guidelines for Merchanting Trade Transactions to facilitate trade by allowing certain processing of goods and setting specific compliance requirements for AD banks. These changes aim to streamline MTT operations while ensuring adherence to KYC and AML guidelines.

obligations.action: Ensure goods acquired for merchanting trade do not enter the Domestic Tariff Area.
obligations.notes: Goods may undergo specific processing if documentary evidence and bonafides are satisfactory.

obligations.action: Ensure MTT goods are permitted for exports/imports under the prevailing Foreign Trade Policy as on the date of shipment.
obligations.notes: Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, and directions for export and import legs.

obligations.action: Satisfy itself with the bonafides of MTT transactions and adhere to KYC and AML guidelines.
Route the entire merchanting trade through the same AD bank and verify trade documents.
obligations.notes: May rely on online verification of Bill of Lading/Airway Bill.

obligations.action: Complete the entire MTT within nine months with no foreign exchange outlay beyond four months.
obligations.notes: Commencement date is the date of shipment/export leg receipt or import leg payment, whichever is first.

obligations.action: Report defaults in any leg of MTT to the concerned Regional Office of the Reserve Bank on a half-yearly basis.
obligations.deadline: within 15 days from the close of each half year, i.e. June and December

obligations.action: Write-off unrealized amount of export leg under specified circumstances.
obligations.notes: Subject to conditions such as insolvency, auction/destruction of goods, or intervention by Indian Embassy.

obligations.action: Ensure one-to-one matching in each MTT and report defaults.
Report merchanting trade transactions under FETERS on a gross basis using specified codes.
obligations.notes: Use Purpose Code P0108 for export and S0108 for import.

key_thresholds.context: Advance payment beyond this amount requires Bank Guarantee or standby Letter of Credit.

key_thresholds.value: 5% or more of annual export earnings

supersedes.circular_reference: A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No.115 dated March 28, 2014
supersedes.description: Supersedes previous guidelines on merchanting trade transactions.

extraction.risk_rationale: The revised guidelines introduce specific compliance requirements and timelines that require careful adherence by AD banks to avoid regulatory issues.

extraction.effective_date: from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette
extraction.subject: Foreign Exchange Management (Export of Goods and Services) (Amendment) Regulations, 2021
extraction.summary: The amendment modifies the interest rate cap on advance payments for exports, setting it to not exceed 100 basis points above LIBOR or another benchmark as directed by the RBI. This change is important for exporters managing advance payments and interest costs.

obligations.action: Ensure the rate of interest on advance payments does not exceed 100 basis points above LIBOR or other applicable benchmark as directed by the RBI.
obligations.notes: This obligation applies to the interest rate on advance payments for exports.

key_thresholds.context: The maximum allowable interest rate for advance payments on exports.

amendments_to.regulation_name: Foreign Exchange Management (Export of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2015

extraction.risk_rationale: Non-compliance could lead to financial discrepancies and potential regulatory scrutiny for exporters.

extraction.effective_date: from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette
extraction.subject: Foreign Exchange Management (Transfer or Issue of Security by a Person Resident outside India) (Thirteenth Amendment) Regulations, 2016
extraction.summary: This amendment to the Foreign Exchange Management Regulations allows 100% foreign investment in 'Other Financial Services' under the automatic route, subject to regulatory conditions. It clarifies the conditions under which foreign investment in financial services activities is permitted, including the need for regulatory oversight and minimum capitalization norms.

applies_to.conditions: Activities must be regulated by a financial sector regulator or require government approval if not fully regulated.

obligations.action: Ensure foreign investment in 'Other Financial Services' is subject to conditionalities, including minimum capitalization norms.
obligations.notes: Applies to financial services activities regulated by RBI, SEBI, IRDA, PFRDA, NHB, or any other notified regulator.

obligations.action: Obtain government approval for foreign investment up to 100% in financial services activities not fully regulated by a financial sector regulator.
obligations.notes: Subject to conditions including minimum capitalization requirement.

obligations.action: Ensure foreign investment limits comply with those specified in any applicable Act for specifically regulated activities.
obligations.notes: Foreign investment limits are restricted to levels specified in the relevant Act.

obligations.action: Ensure downstream investments by entities engaged in 'Other Financial Services' comply with extant sectoral regulations and provisions of the Foreign Exchange Management Regulations.
obligations.notes: Subject to amendments from time to time.

key_thresholds.context: Allowed under automatic route for regulated 'Other Financial Services' activities.

supersedes.description: Amends Schedule 1, Annex B, Paragraph F.8 of the original regulations.

amendments_to.regulation_name: Foreign Exchange Management (Transfer or Issue of Security by a Person Resident outside India) Regulations, 2000

extraction.risk_rationale: The amendment introduces new conditions for foreign investment in financial services, requiring compliance with regulatory oversight and capitalization norms, which may pose moderate compliance challenges.
